  • The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x={\color{blue}{1}}] to [MATH: x=2.]

sections.normalized_html: Find the total area of the region between the curve [MATH: y=\dfrac{1}{2}x^3] and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-1] to [MATH: x=\dfrac{3}{2}.]
sections.readable_text:
Find the total area of the region between the curve [MATH: y=\dfrac{1}{2}x^3] and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-1] to [MATH: x=\dfrac{3}{2}.]

[IMG: /graphics/ba25ac7d1486034bfea03158e8407dae]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the [MATH: x]-axis:

[MATH: (1)/(2)x^{3}|= 0; x^{3}|= 0; x|= 0.]

Since [MATH: 0 \in \left[-1,\dfrac{3}{2}\right]], we have two regions:

  • The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-1] to [MATH: x=0.]

  • The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=0] to [MATH: x=\dfrac{3}{2}.]

Notice that for [MATH: x \in [-1,0]] the region lies completely below the [MATH: x]-axis. Hence, the value of [MATH: \int_{a}^{b} y(x) \:\textrm{d}x = \int_{-1}^{0} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x] will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by [MATH: A_1 = -\int_{-1}^{0} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x .]

For [MATH: x \in\left[0,\dfrac{3}{2}\right]], we have [MATH: A_2 = \int_{0}^{3/2}\dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x.]

The total area is [MATH: A = A_1+A_2 = - \int_{-1}^{0} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x + \int_{0}^{3/2} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x .]

Finally, we carry out the integration:

[MATH: A|= − ∫_{− 1}^{0}(x^{3})/(2)dx + ∫_{0}^{3/2}(x^{3})/(2)dx; = − [(x^{4})/(8)]_{− 1}^{0} + [(x^{4})/(8)]_{0}^{3/2}; = − [0 − (1)/(8)] + [(81)/(128) − 0]; = (1)/(8) + (81)/(128); = (97)/(128)]

sections.normalized_html: Find the total area of the region between the curve [MATH: y=x^3-9x] and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-3] to [MATH: x=3.]
sections.readable_text: Find the total area of the region between the curve [MATH: y=x^3-9x] and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-3] to [MATH: x=3.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the [MATH: x]-axis: [MATH: x^{3} − 9x|= 0; x(x^{2} − 9)|= 0; x(x − 3)(x + 3)|= 0]

Therefore, [MATH: x=0,] [MATH: x=-3,] and [MATH: x=3] are our real solutions. Since [MATH: 0 \in [-3,3]], we have two regions:

  • The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-3] to [MATH: x=0.]

  • The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=0] to [MATH: x=3.]

For [MATH: x \in [-3,0]], we obtain [MATH: A_{1}|= ∫_{a}^{b}y(x)dx; = ∫_{− 3}^{0}(x^{3} − 9x)dx; = ∫_{− 3}^{0}x^{3}dx − 9∫_{− 3}^{0}xdx; = (x^{4})/(4)|_{− 3}^{0} − (9x^{2})/(2)|_{− 3}^{0}; = [0 − ((− 3)^{4})/(4)] − 9[0 − ((− 3)^{2})/(2)]; = − (81)/(4) + (81)/(2); = (81)/(4).]

Notice that for [MATH: x \in [0,3]] the region lies completely below the [MATH: x]-axis. Hence, the value of [MATH: \int_{a}^{b} y(x) \:\textrm{d}x = \int_{0}^{3} \left(x^3-9x\right) \:\textrm{d}x] will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by [MATH: A_{2}|= − ∫_{0}^{3}(x^{3} − 9x)dx; = − ∫_{0}^{3}x^{3}dx + 9∫_{0}^{3}xdx; = − (x^{4})/(4)|_{0}^{3} + (9x^{2})/(2)|_{0}^{3}; = − [((3)^{4})/(4) − 0] + 9[((3)^{2})/(2) − 0]; = − (81)/(4) + (81)/(2); = (81)/(4).]

Finally, the total area is [MATH: A = A_1+A_2 = \dfrac{81}{4} + \dfrac{81}{4} = \dfrac{81}{2}.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When we compute the area between a curve [MATH: y=y(x)] and the [MATH: x]-axis using integration, we must bear the following in mind:

Content:
- definite integrals that correspond to areas above the [MATH: x]-axis are positive,
- definite integrals that correspond to areas below the [MATH: x]-axis are negative.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cbda894accfb4a70ea0f06b3a461eb37]

Content:
The facts above become crucial when we attempt to find the area bounded by a curve that crosses the [MATH: x]-axis.

---

Item 2 — Example: Constructing an Integral That Gives the Area Bounded by a Curve

Example Prompt:
The total area [MATH: A] of the region between the curve [MATH: y=x^3-1] and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-2] to [MATH: x=2] is given by the integral expression below. What is the value of [MATH: a?]
[MATH: A = \displaystyle -\int_{-2}^{a} (x^3-1) \:\textrm{d}x + \int_{a}^{2} (x^3-1) \:\textrm{d}x]

[IMG: /graphics/57a34212c16bef10ef454f07479d2053]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To determine the missing limit of integration, we need to find the [MATH: x]-intercept of the curve [MATH: y=x^3-1.] So, we set [MATH: y=0] and solve for [MATH: x] as follows:

[MATH: y|= x^{3} − 1; (0)|= x^{3} − 1; x^{3}|= 1; x|= 1.]

Since [MATH: 1 \in [-2,2]], we have two regions:

- The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-2] to [MATH: x={\color{blue}{1}}.]
- The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x={\color{blue}{1}}] to [MATH: x=2.]

So, [MATH: a={\color{blue}1}] and the final expression will be
[MATH: A = \displaystyle -\int_{-2}^{\color{blue}1} (x^3-1) \:\textrm{d}x + \int_{\color{blue}1}^{2} (x^3-1) \:\textrm{d}x.]

---

Item 5 — Example: Finding the Total Area Bounded Between the X-Axis and a Curve

Example Prompt:
Find the total area of the region between the curve [MATH: y=\dfrac{1}{2}x^3] and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-1] to [MATH: x=\dfrac{3}{2}.]

[IMG: /graphics/ba25ac7d1486034bfea03158e8407dae]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the [MATH: x]-axis:

[MATH: (1)/(2)x^{3}|= 0; x^{3}|= 0; x|= 0.]

Since [MATH: 0 \in \left[-1,\dfrac{3}{2}\right]], we have two regions:

- The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-1] to [MATH: x=0.]
- The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=0] to [MATH: x=\dfrac{3}{2}.]

Notice that for [MATH: x \in [-1,0]] the region lies completely below the [MATH: x]-axis. Hence, the value of
[MATH: \int_{a}^{b} y(x) \:\textrm{d}x = \int_{-1}^{0} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x]
will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by
[MATH: A_1 = -\int_{-1}^{0} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x .]

For [MATH: x \in\left[0,\dfrac{3}{2}\right]], we have
[MATH: A_2 = \int_{0}^{3/2}\dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x.]

The total area is
[MATH: A = A_1+A_2 = - \int_{-1}^{0} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x + \int_{0}^{3/2} \dfrac{x^3}{2} \:\textrm{d}x .]

Finally, we carry out the integration:

[MATH: A|= − ∫_{− 1}^{0}(x^{3})/(2)dx + ∫_{0}^{3/2}(x^{3})/(2)dx; = − [(x^{4})/(8)]_{− 1}^{0} + [(x^{4})/(8)]_{0}^{3/2}; = − [0 − (1)/(8)] + [(81)/(128) − 0]; = (1)/(8) + (81)/(128); = (97)/(128)]

Item 8 — Example: Finding the Total Area Bounded By a Curve When It Crosses the X-Axis Several Times

Example Prompt:
Find the total area of the region between the curve [MATH: y=x^3-9x] and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-3] to [MATH: x=3.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the [MATH: x]-axis:
[MATH: x^{3} − 9x|= 0; x(x^{2} − 9)|= 0; x(x − 3)(x + 3)|= 0]

Therefore, [MATH: x=0,] [MATH: x=-3,] and [MATH: x=3] are our real solutions. Since [MATH: 0 \in [-3,3]], we have two regions:

- The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=-3] to [MATH: x=0.]
- The area between the curve and the [MATH: x]-axis from [MATH: x=0] to [MATH: x=3.]

[IMG: /graphics/2a563bcdf5a67c69214ca4fcde498ea4]

For [MATH: x \in [-3,0]], we obtain
[MATH: A_{1}|= ∫_{a}^{b}y(x)dx; = ∫_{− 3}^{0}(x^{3} − 9x)dx; = ∫_{− 3}^{0}x^{3}dx − 9∫_{− 3}^{0}xdx; = (x^{4})/(4)|_{− 3}^{0} − (9x^{2})/(2)|_{− 3}^{0}; = [0 − ((− 3)^{4})/(4)] − 9[0 − ((− 3)^{2})/(2)]; = − (81)/(4) + (81)/(2); = (81)/(4).]

Notice that for [MATH: x \in [0,3]] the region lies completely below the [MATH: x]-axis. Hence, the value of
[MATH: \int_{a}^{b} y(x) \:\textrm{d}x = \int_{0}^{3} \left(x^3-9x\right) \:\textrm{d}x]
will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by
[MATH: A_{2}|= − ∫_{0}^{3}(x^{3} − 9x)dx; = − ∫_{0}^{3}x^{3}dx + 9∫_{0}^{3}xdx; = − (x^{4})/(4)|_{0}^{3} + (9x^{2})/(2)|_{0}^{3}; = − [((3)^{4})/(4) − 0] + 9[((3)^{2})/(2) − 0]; = − (81)/(4) + (81)/(2); = (81)/(4).]

Finally, the total area is
[MATH: A = A_1+A_2 = \dfrac{81}{4} + \dfrac{81}{4} = \dfrac{81}{2}.]
